content:
In #40214 I took a look at the places in Mathlib where omega cannot be directly replaced by lia, as reported at #nightly-testing-mathlib > nightly-testing regression log. About 75% of these appear to be because lia does not see docs#max_def and docs#min_def. You can easily use grind here, but this is somewhat of a regression.

At the same time, there is an interesting docstring on docs#Lean.Grind.CutsatConfig that is maybe relevant:

Note: cutsat benefits from some amount of instantiation, e.g. [Nat.max_def](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Init/Data/Nat/Basic.html#Nat.max_def). We don't currently have a mechanism to enable only a small set of lemmas.

Does this mean that in the future there might be a way to configure lia with some very light instantiation like max_def and min_def? Or is this scope creep and just a difference between omega and lia?
Hmm, maybe something to consider after #39370, which hopefully can be reviewed soon.
I'm implementing @[lia] in lean4 now, and telling lia to use it, and will add the attribute to a few obvious things in Init.
(This was an oversight that it hasn't already been done; I dropped the ball after register_grind_attr was implemented.)
Oh I see, I think I misunderstood above. And no worries, thanks for taking a look!
